item.content:encoded:
Dezeen School Shows: a lamp crafted from minimally processed wood is among designs by participants of New Designers that will be displayed during the London Design Festival this year.

Also included is a mirror framed with a distinctive ripple-like structure, and candle holders sculpted from coloured porcelain.

New Designers

Institution: New Designers

School statement:

"New Designers Selects (ND Selects) is heading to Shoreditch this September, bringing a new generation of emerging design talent to the heart of London Design Festival.

"For the first time outside New Designers' flagship July showcase, ND Selects at Shoreditch Design Week will present a curated selection of young design businesses, typically one to five years into their careers.

"Running from 15 to 17 September 2026 at Kachette, 347 Old Street, the showcase is a new collaboration between New Designers and Shoreditch Design Week.

"The event will take place in what will be London Design Festival's biggest district and offering emerging practices a platform to connect with the wider design industry."

Hem Stool by Dan Davies Design

"I am a recent furniture design graduate from Nottingham Trent University, specialising in material-led, process-driven design.

"My work explores sustainability, circular principles and honest manufacturing, with a focus on creating refined, functional pieces that are built to last.

"I currently work as a circular designer at Lamington Group, designing furniture and products using reclaimed and waste materials.

"My practice combines hands-on making with an understanding of production, aiming to create efficient, durable designs with a clear and considered aesthetic."

Designer: Dan Davies Design
Course: Furniture Design
Email: info[at]dandaviesdesign.com

Serene Table Lamp by Jasmine Prime

"Jasmine is a product and furniture designer from London. Her practice explores the intersection of traditional craft and contemporary design, with a focus on natural materials and traditional techniques.

"She works predominantly with minimally processed woods and other organic materials, allowing their inherent qualities to guide form, structure and function.

"Her work often involves adapting time-honoured techniques to new typologies, seeking to preserve craft knowledge while giving it a new relevance within today's material culture.

"Through this approach, Jasmine aims to create high-quality contemporary furniture and objects that celebrate craftsmanship, longevity, and the expressive potential of natural materials."

Designer: Jasmine Prime
Course: Product and Furniture Design

Crackdown by Studio Soldout x LightOn Lighting

"Studio Soldout is an Istanbul-based design studio founded by industrial designer Ibrahim Fatih Satılmış.

"The studio develops lighting, furniture and objects with a focus on contemporary minimalism, cultural depth and production-ready detailing.

"Its work explores the relationship between material, light, form and atmosphere. Rather than treating decoration as surface detail, Studio Soldout approaches each object as a functional piece with a clear spatial presence.

"Materials such as metal, glass, stone and ceramic are often used to create calm, tactile and refined objects for contemporary interiors.

"The studio's process combines concept development, 3D CAD modelling, visualisation, CMF development, prototyping and manufacturing alignment.

"This allows each project to move from an initial idea to a technically considered object that can be presented, produced or developed further with manufacturers.

"Recent works include Crackdown, an award-winning decorative lighting object, and Moonside, a side table and lighting concept exploring transformation, wireless charging and changing light direction through a moon-inspired form.

"Through these projects, Studio Soldout continues to build a design language that is minimal, culturally aware and suitable for international design contexts."

Design studio: Studio Soldout x LightOn Lighting
Course: Product Design
Email: info[at]studiosoldout.com

Dune Candle Holder by Riolab Ceramics

"Riolab Ceramics is a London-based design studio founded by Chilean industrial designer Paulina Moreno Rios.

"With a background in industrial design, the studio explores the intersection between digital technologies and traditional craft, creating contemporary ceramic pieces that are both sculptural and functional.

"Working primarily with coloured porcelain, Paulina develops objects that celebrate form, texture and colour.

"Her process balances technology and experimentation with artisanal craftsmanship, blending slip-casting and hand-finishing to create objects full of character and tactile presence.

"Her latest collection, Dune, is inspired by the desert landscapes of northern Chile, where she grew up. The surfaces of the pieces reflect the movement of sand shaped by wind and light, where tonal variations shift from warm oranges and browns in daylight to deeper purples at sunset.

"With this collection, she aims to invite touch and evoke a sense of movement. The shadows across the surface of the pieces enhance this effect, encouraging people to explore and connect with these tactile objects."

Design studio: Riolab Ceramics
Course: Ceramics
Email: riolabceramica[at]gmail.com

What Holds by Irenehuang.Design

"My practice focuses on material-led furniture mainly with wood and ceramic.

"Through functional objects, I explore domestic space, material relationships, and how everyday use shapes meaning, memory and lived experience."

Design studio: Irenehuang.Design
Course: Furniture Design
Email: huangzixun530[at]gmail.com

Pure Apricity Lamp by Rosie May Ceramics

"Driven by a passion for lighting, my practice explores how light influences the emotional quality of an interior setting.

"Influenced by principles of biophilic design, my work considers how natural references can be reintroduced into contemporary interiors through form, texture, and tactility.

"Rather than directly replicating natural forms, I translate their rhythms and irregularities through developed processes that allow subtle variations in form and surface.

"My practice is fundamentally process-led. Through making, I investigate how material, thickness, and surface alter the behaviour of light.

"Working primarily with porcelain, I am drawn to its delicate yet durable nature and the way its translucency diffuses light.

"Using slipcasting as a method of control and experimentation, I refine wall thickness and surface detail to achieve a soft, ambient glow. Each piece evolves through refinement, balancing precision with organic form.

"Positioned between craft and contemporary lighting design, my work explores how porcelain and light can be used deliberately to define the character of a space."

Designer: Rosie May Ceramics
Course: Product Design and Ceramics
Email: rosiemaymarks[at]gmail.com

Kruller Midi Mirror | Walnut by This is Oink

"We're Lulu and Dan, co-founders of This is Oink, a design studio making home and bespoke goods from our workshop on a Dorset farm.

"Dan is a product designer and skilled maker, while Lulu is a graphic designer; together we've developed our craft at notable studios and major institutions across London and Melbourne over the past decade.

"Our creative practice grows through a process of experimentation, combining traditional craft values with the possibilities of modern machinery.

"We launched with our Kruller Mirror collection, characterised by its distinctive ripple form across a variety of timbers and sizes. Alongside this, our Timbre collection explores material contrast through turned bowls and our Timbre Lamp, defined by a continuous wiggle joint.

"Our work is rooted in process, combining traditional craftsmanship with modern machining to create playful yet refined objects for the home."

Design studio: This is Oink
Course: Product Design
Email: info[at]thisisoink.com

Tranquility by Ceramakka

"Ceramakka explores how sculptural form can bring the restorative qualities of nature into contemporary interiors.

"Inspired by the Japanese practice of Shinrin-yoku (Forest Bathing), Louisa Akka creates biomorphic ceramic forms that echo the cycles of growth, entropy and regeneration found in the natural world.

"Working with clay as an elemental and responsive material, each piece is shaped to create a quiet dialogue between form, light, shadow and space.

"The unglazed surfaces reveal the natural beauty of the ceramic material, with some sculptures meticulously hand-sanded to a silky, tactile finish, while others use a signature iron-transfer technique to evoke organic textures and tonal qualities of the forest.

"Material integrity and sustainability are integral to the practice, with single firings, no glazes and recycling of armature components.

"Created for residential, hospitality and architectural environments, Ceramakka sits at the intersection of contemporary craft and biophilic design, inviting a slower, more sensory engagement with space."

Design studio: Ceramakka
Course: Ceramics
Email: louisa[at]moorgate-orient.co.uk

Frame Stool by Caden Hao

"The goal of my design project is to create artefacts that invite introspection, presence and perspective.

"Within the concept of introspection, I'm creating objects that spark the practice of examining one's own thoughts and emotions to gain deeper self-awareness and understanding.

"This project is an exploration of how design can gently shift our attention inward, encouraging presence and inviting reflective practice.

"This collection of wooden furniture explores tactility, inviting a more embodied and intuitive way of sensing. A shallow inner slope on the sitting surface remains visually subtle, revealing itself only through physical engagement.

"The contrast between its visual lightness and actual weight prompts a moment of pause when lifting the piece.

"By creating tension between what is seen and what is felt, the work draws attention to the present and shifts focus away from purely visual perception."

Student: Caden Hao
Course: Furniture Design
Email: cadenhao522[at]gmail.com

Conchiolin Console Table by Phil Berczuk Design

"My creative practice sits at the intersection of the natural and the constructed.

"It draws on organic forms, raw materials and elemental processes, as well as the geometry and texture of the built environment, transforming these influences into singular pieces of sculptural furniture.

"The Conchiolin Series is inspired by the protective layered architecture of giant clam and oyster shells, exploring ideas of growth and transformation.

"Constructed from micro-laminated smoked oak veneer, the pieces are hand sculpted into linear rhythmic forms, delicately balanced across multiple components."

Student: Phil Berczuk Design
Course: Product and Furniture Design
Email: phil[at]philberczuk.design

item.content:encoded:
Accoya wood cladding and expansive terraces feature at the Dune House, which was designed by American studio Ziger Snead Architects for a tight site with many restrictions.

Tucked into a dense area, the home is located on Fenwick Island – a long, slender strip of land found just off the coast of Delaware.

The home fits a "demanding program on a sensitive site with a tight zoning envelope", said Baltimore-based Ziger Snead Architects.

The project was designed for a family who had summered on Fenwick Island for decades and desired a vacation home rooted to place.

"When they acquired a rare corner lot overlooking the dunes, they sought a home that would accommodate their growing family while fostering deep connections with the surrounding landscape," the architecture studio said.

The team conceived a bar-shaped, three-storey building that adheres to a 35-foot (10.7-metre) height restriction.

Along the east elevation, wide terraces cantilever over the beach and look toward the Atlantic Ocean. At the very top, the roof extends outward to form a trellis-like eave.

Facades are clad in a accoya wood that is meant to age over time.

"Left unfinished, the accoya weathers in the salt air, allowing the house to age in the landscape and contain time and place in its materiality," the team said.

Read:

Slate House by Ziger Snead replaces fire-ravaged Maryland home

Some areas of the exterior are lined with wooden slats, which "create a light, airy facade that softens the silhouette and generates shifting patterns of light and shadow throughout the day".

The house is entered on the ground level, which could potentially flood, prompting the team to avoid placing main living spaces there.

Instead, a mudroom, garage and gym occupy the bottom level, along with elements for beach living — outdoor showers, foot-washing stations and storage space for paddleboards and beach umbrellas.

"By elevating living spaces above the floodplain and using breakaway construction at ground level, the design also provides flood resilience," the team said.

The middle floor holds a lounge and four bedrooms, each with ocean views and access to terraces. The top floor encompasses the communal zone and primary bedroom.

"At the upper level, the house opens entirely," the team said. "The living, dining and entertaining spaces occupy a vast, open area that extends onto a terrace cantilevering 17 feet over the dunes."

Throughout the interior, one finds a restrained selection of materials and colours.

"The palette is muted and reserved, focusing attention on the views and surroundings," the team said.

Several custom pieces have a strong connection to place. For instance, sinks and a coffee table are made of concrete with sand from the adjacent beach. The dining table is crafted from a fallen ash tree in Baltimore, where the family is based.

Other projects by Ziger Snead Architects include a family home in Maryland with stone shingles and charred wood on the exterior. It was built to replace a ranch-style home that was lost in a fire.

The photography is by Jennifer Hughes.
